    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 1,
            "text": "# Tool Registry + Executor System"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3,
            "text": "This directory implements the Tool Registry + Executor system for Atlas, which provides a unified interface for executing tools."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 5,
            "text": "## Architecture"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 7,
            "text": "### 1. Tool Registry (&#96;tools_registry.json&#96;)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9,
            "text": "A JSON file that catalogs all available tools with metadata:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 10,
            "text": "- **name**: Tool identifier"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11,
            "text": "- **description**: What the tool does"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 12,
            "text": "- **inputs**: Required/optional arguments with types"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 13,
            "text": "- **output**: What the tool returns"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14,
            "text": "- **when_to_use**: Examples of when to use this tool"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15,
            "text": "- **when_not_to_use**: Examples of when NOT to use"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16,
            "text": "- **cost/latency**: Performance characteristics"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17,
            "text": "- **dependencies**: Required resources (internet, API keys, etc.)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19,
            "text": "### 2. Tool Executor (&#96;tool_executor.py&#96;)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 21,
            "text": "A single interface that executes any tool by name:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;python"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23,
            "text": "from atlas_client.router import execute_tool"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25,
            "text": "result = await execute_tool(\"web_search\", {\"query\": \"latest news\"}, state)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28,
            "text": "The executor:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29,
            "text": "- Validates tool exists in registry"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30,
            "text": "- Validates required arguments"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31,
            "text": "- Calls the appropriate tool implementation"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32,
            "text": "- Returns standardized result format: &#96;{ok, tool, summary, data, error}&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34,
            "text": "### 3. Integration (&#96;orchestrator.py&#96;)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36,
            "text": "The orchestrator:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37,
            "text": "1. Receives user input"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 38,
            "text": "2. Model decides tool usage via instructions (see &#96;tool_instructions.py&#96;)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 39,
            "text": "3. Parses tool calls from model output"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 40,
            "text": "4. Executes tools via &#96;execute_tool()&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 41,
            "text": "5. Model generates final response"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 43,
            "text": "## Flow Example"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 46,
            "text": "User: \"What's the latest news about AI?\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 48,
            "text": "1. Model receives user input with tool instructions"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 49,
            "text": "2. Model decides to call web_search tool"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 50,
            "text": "3. Model outputs: {\"type\":\"tool\",\"name\":\"web_search\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"latest news about AI\"}}"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 51,
            "text": "4. Orchestrator parses tool call"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 52,
            "text": "5. Executor runs web_search tool"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 53,
            "text": "6. For web_search: results are re-ingested, model generates final answer"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 54,
            "text": "7. TTS speaks response"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57,
            "text": "## Adding a New Tool"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 59,
            "text": "1. **Add to registry** (&#96;tools_registry.json&#96;):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 60,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;json"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 61,
            "text": "{"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 62,
            "text": "  \"name\": \"my_tool\","
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 63,
            "text": "  \"description\": \"What it does\","
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 64,
            "text": "  \"inputs\": {...},"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 65,
            "text": "  ..."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 66,
            "text": "}"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 67,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69,
            "text": "2. **Implement in executor** (&#96;tool_executor.py&#96;):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 70,
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;python"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71,
            "text": "elif name == \"my_tool\":"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 72,
            "text": "    # Extract args"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73,
            "text": "    # Call tool implementation"
          }
        ],
        "range": {
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 73
          },
          "startPosition": {}
        },
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\src\\work\\atlas\\src\\atlas_client\\router\\README.md",
        "signatures": {}
      },
      "score": 0.2384476661682129
    },
    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 108,
            "text": "def search_items("
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 109,
            "text": "    query: Optional[str] = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 110,
            "text": "    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 111,
            "text": "    status: Optional[str] = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 112,
            "text": "    limit: int = 10,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 113,
            "text": "    due_before: Optional[str] = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 114,
            "text": "    due_after: Optional[str] = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 115,
            "text": "    created_before: Optional[str] = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 116,
            "text": "    created_after: Optional[str] = None"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 117,
            "text": ") -\u003e List[Dict[str, Any]]:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 118,
            "text": "    \"\"\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 119,
            "text": "    Search for memory items."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 120,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 121,
            "text": "    Args:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 122,
            "text": "        query: Text search query (searches in 'text' field)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 123,
            "text": "        tags: Filter by tags (any of the provided tags)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 124,
            "text": "        status: Filter by status (open/done/archived)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 125,
            "text": "        limit: Maximum number of results"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 126,
            "text": "        due_before: Filter items with due_at before this ISO datetime"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 127,
            "text": "        due_after: Filter items with due_at after this ISO datetime"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 128,
            "text": "        created_before: Filter items with created_at before this ISO datetime"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 129,
            "text": "        created_after: Filter items with created_at after this ISO datetime"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 130,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 131,
            "text": "    Returns:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 132,
            "text": "        List of matching items"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 133,
            "text": "    \"\"\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 134,
            "text": "    _init_db()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 135,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 136,
            "text": "    conditions = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 137,
            "text": "    params = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 138,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 139,
            "text": "    if query:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 140,
            "text": "        conditions.append(\"text LIKE ?\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 141,
            "text": "        params.append(f\"%{query}%\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 142,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 143,
            "text": "    if tags:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 144,
            "text": "        # Search for items that have any of the specified tags"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 145,
            "text": "        tag_conditions = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 146,
            "text": "        for tag in tags:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 147,
            "text": "            tag_conditions.append(\"tags LIKE ?\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 148,
            "text": "            params.append(f'%\"{tag}\"%')"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 149,
            "text": "        if tag_conditions:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 150,
            "text": "            conditions.append(f\"({' OR '.join(tag_conditions)})\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 151,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 152,
            "text": "    if status:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 153,
            "text": "        conditions.append(\"status = ?\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 154,
            "text": "        params.append(status)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 155,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 156,
            "text": "    if due_before:"
          },

      "codeBlock": {
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 66,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/services/pulse_meter.py&#96; contains &#96;main()&#96; but is started by the API via &#96;pulse_manager&#96; (not intended to be run directly)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 68,
            "text": "## The big picture runtime flow (from wake to spoken answer)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 70,
            "text": "### 1) Wake service detects phrase → calls the API"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 72,
            "text": "File: &#96;src/wake_service/main.py&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 74,
            "text": "- Uses &#96;sounddevice.RawInputStream&#96; to capture mic PCM16 audio at 16kHz."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75,
            "text": "- Uses Vosk &#96;KaldiRecognizer&#96; with a **very small grammar** (wake + sleep phrases + &#96;[unk]&#96;)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 76,
            "text": "- On partial and final recognition hits, POSTs JSON:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77,
            "text": "  - POST &#96;WAKE_ENDPOINT&#96; (defaults to API &#96;/wake&#96;) with &#96;{\"intent\":\"wake\"}&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 78,
            "text": "  - POST &#96;SLEEP_ENDPOINT&#96; (defaults to API &#96;/sleep&#96;) with &#96;{\"intent\":\"sleep\"}&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 79,
            "text": "- Uses cooldown + “N partial hits” gating to reduce false triggers."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 81,
            "text": "### 2) Flask API receives &#96;/wake&#96; → starts an assistant session (background thread)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 83,
            "text": "File: &#96;src/atlas_client/app/api.py&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85,
            "text": "Key endpoints:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87,
            "text": "- &#96;GET /&#96;: serves &#96;src/atlas_client/ui/static/index.html&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 88,
            "text": "- &#96;GET /health&#96;: returns &#96;{ok, session_active, session_state, pulse_running}&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89,
            "text": "- &#96;GET /ui&#96;: returns the current UI state dict (&#96;atlas_client.ui.ui_state&#96;)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 90,
            "text": "- &#96;GET /image-search&#96;: calls SerpAPI Google Images and returns URL list"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91,
            "text": "- &#96;GET /image-proxy&#96;: proxies image bytes for the UI (to avoid CORS/hotlink issues)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 92,
            "text": "- &#96;POST /wake&#96;: starts session if not already active:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93,
            "text": "  - starts the **pulse meter subprocess**"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 94,
            "text": "  - spawns a thread that runs &#96;core.main.run_session()&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 95,
            "text": "- &#96;POST /sleep&#96;: signals the session to stop and stops pulse"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 96,
            "text": "- &#96;POST /shutdown&#96;: stops pulse, signals stop, then terminates the API process via &#96;os.kill(os.getpid(), SIGTERM)&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98,
            "text": "Concurrency note:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 100,
            "text": "- &#96;_session_active&#96; + &#96;_session_lock&#96; prevent multiple concurrent sessions. If &#96;/wake&#96; is called while active, it simply ensures pulse is running and returns &#96;already_active&#96;."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 102,
            "text": "### 3) &#96;run_session()&#96; creates an asyncio loop and runs &#96;session_main()&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 104,
            "text": "File: &#96;src/atlas_client/core/main.py&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 106,
            "text": "- Creates a new asyncio event loop in the background thread"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 107,
            "text": "- Installs it into global session state (&#96;set_loop&#96;, &#96;set_stop_event&#96;)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 108,
            "text": "- Runs &#96;loop.run_until_complete(session_main())&#96;"
          }
        ],

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was wired up.

### Where Atlas stores memory
- **SQLite**: `src/work/atlas/data/atlas_memory.sqlite` (from `atlas_client.storage.memory_store`).
- Table **`memory_items`**: `id`, `text`, `tags` (JSON array), `due_at`, `status` (`open` / `done` / etc.), timestamps.

### Backend
- **`backend/product_shell/services/atlas_memory_reader.py`**  
  - Reads that DB (read-only).  
  - **`ATLAS_MEMORY_SQLITE`** env var can override the path.
- **`GET /api/memory/projects`**  
  - Builds groups from **tags**: always **`All items`** (`__all__`), then one entry per tag that appears on any row (with counts).
- **`GET /api/memory/tasks?project_id=...`**  
  - **`__all__`**: every item (newest first, cap 500).  
  - **Any other `project_id`**: items whose **`tags`** include that string (same as Atlas tag names).

**Schemas** now include optional **`count`** on projects and **`tags`, `due_at`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`** on tasks.

### Frontend (**Memory** mode)
- Loads **real** projects/tasks from the API.
- Resets selection if the old id (e.g. demo `atlas`) isn’t in the new list; default is **`All items`**.
- Shows **text**, **tag chips**, **due** (when `due_at` is set), **status** when relevant.
- Copy explains data comes from the **Atlas memory store**.

### Note
There is no separate “project” table in Atlas—**tags** are what create the groups (e.g. `todo`, `reminder`, `note`, or anything you pass to `memory_add`). Items with **no shared tags** still show under **All items** only.

If the DB file is missing or empty, you’ll see **All items (0)** and an empty list until something is saved via Atlas (`memory_add`, etc.).

Here’s what was added.

### Storage (CSPE, not Atlas)
- **SQLite file:** `data/product_memory.sqlite` (created automatically; `data/` stays gitignored as before).
- **`projects`:** `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
- **`project_items`:** `id`, `project_id` (FK, cascade delete), `title`, **`status`** `todo` | `in_progress` | `done`, timestamps.

Atlas **`memory_items`** is unchanged; this is the **product** task board only.

### API (`backend/product_shell/`)
- **`GET /api/memory/projects`** — list projects + item counts.
- **`POST /api/memory/projects`** — body `{ "name": "..." }`.
- **`PATCH /api/memory/projects/{id}`** — rename (`{ "name": "..." }`) — ready for UI later.
- **`DELETE /api/memory/projects/{id}`** — delete project and all its items.
- **`GET /api/memory/tasks?project_id=`** — list items for one project.
- **`POST /api/memory/tasks`** — `{ "project_id", "title", "status"? }` (default `todo`).
- **`PATCH /api/memory/tasks/{id}`** — `{ "title"?, "status"? }`.
- **`DELETE /api/memory/tasks/{id}`**.

Implementation: **`services/product_memory_store.py`**. **`atlas_memory_reader.py`** is still in the repo but **no longer used** by these routes.

### Schemas
- Tasks expose **`status`** as `todo` | `in_progress` | `done` and **`done`** (`true` when `status === "done"`).

### UI (Memory mode)
- **Right float:** name field + **Add project**, list of projects (select + **Del**).
- **Main:** after a project is selected — **Add item**, list with **Status** dropdown (To do / In progress / Done), **Remove** per row.

_**User**_

do we actually have a database where we store this, in what format?

---

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Yes. **Projects and items from the Memory page** are stored in a **SQLite** database on disk.

### Location
- **File:** `data/product_memory.sqlite`  
- **Resolved from repo root:** `C:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\data\product_memory.sqlite`  
- The `data/` folder is normally **gitignored**, so the file is **local** to your machine (not committed).

### Format
- **Engine:** SQLite 3 (single `.sqlite` file).
- **Tables:**
  - **`projects`** — `id` (integer PK), `name` (text), `created_at`, `updated_at` (ISO-8601 text).
  - **`project_items`** — `id` (integer PK), `project_id` (FK → `projects.id`, **ON DELETE CASCADE**), `title` (text), `status` (`'todo' | 'in_progress' | 'done'`), `created_at`, `updated_at`.

Defined in:

```38:51:c:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\backend\product_shell\services\product_memory_store.py
        c.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projects (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS project_items (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
                title TEXT NOT NULL,
                status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo'
                    CHECK (status IN ('todo', 'in_progress', 'done')),
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
            );
```

### Not the same as Atlas memory
Atlas’s **notes/reminders** still live in **`src/work/atlas/data/atlas_memory.sqlite`** (`memory_items` table). The product **projects/tasks** DB is **separate** unless you later build a sync between them.

### Done
1. **`store.ts`** — Restored correct image state: `knowledgeImages: images.length ? images : s.knowledgeImages` (and same idea for panels). No more broken ternary.
2. **`ToolRail.tsx`** — Dropped the Knowledge button. Order is **Transport → Visual → Memory**. The **same grid/board SVG** is still used for `visual`; tooltip/label is **“Search and visuals”** so it reads as one search/info surface.

4. **`VisualBoardMode.tsx`** — Single layout: **center** = deduped gallery from `knowledgeImages` + panel URLs; **right** = `knowledgeSummary` plus optional **Panel notes** (titles/queries when present).
5. **`KnowledgeMode.tsx`** — Removed as unused.
6. **`npm run build`** — Succeeds.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
`/api/chat` uses `send_text_and_wait`, which stopped as soon as the **assistant message** was unchanged for several polls (~2s). In Atlas, **image panels often update after** the assistant text stops changing (search/tools finish later). So the API returned a snapshot **before** URLs were in `panels`. On the **next** message, the pre-send `/ui` read already included those URLs, so normalization produced `image_results` for the **previous** turn.

### Fix
In `atlas_http.py`, after assistant text is considered stable we run a short **panel settle** phase: keep polling for up to ~22s (still capped by the overall deadline) until the **panel JSON** is unchanged for several polls in a row. Then we return that UI so `normalize_atlas_ui` sees the same images the user expects for the current turn.

```97:145:c:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\backend\product_shell\services\atlas_http.py
    def _wait_panel_settle(
        ui: dict[str, Any], *, grace_s: float = 22.0, panel_stable_need: int = 4
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Keep polling after assistant text settled; image panels often update later."""
        ...
                if stable >= stable_need:
                    last_ui = _wait_panel_settle(last_ui)
                    return last_ui, None
```

Restart the product shell (or whatever serves `backend/product_shell`) so this code is loaded. If some image-heavy replies still need more time, we can raise `grace_s` or `panel_stable_need` slightly.

          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 228,
            "text": "def plot_graph_3d("
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 229,
            "text": "    G: nx.Graph,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 230,
            "text": "    pos: dict[str, tuple[float, float]],"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 231,
            "text": "    path: list[str] | None = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 232,
            "text": "    *,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 233,
            "text": "    focus_nodes: list[str] | None = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 234,
            "text": "    highlight_mode: str | None = None,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 235,
            "text": "    max_nodes: int = 4000,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 236,
            "text": "    focus_hops: int = 2,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 237,
            "text": "    show_transfers: bool = True,"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 238,
            "text": "):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 239,
            "text": "    H = _focus_subgraph(G, focus_nodes=focus_nodes, path=path, max_nodes=max_nodes, hops=focus_hops)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 240,
            "text": "    local_pos = _local_map_positions(H, pos)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 241,
            "text": "    path_edges = _path_edge_set(path)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 242,
            "text": "    path_nodes = {str(node) for node in (path or []) if str(node) in H}"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 243,
            "text": "    focus_node_set = {str(node) for node in (focus_nodes or []) if str(node) in H}"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 245,
            "text": "    grouped_edges: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 246,
            "text": "    highlighted_edges: list[tuple[str, str]] = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 248,
            "text": "    for u, v, data in H.edges(data=True):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 249,
            "text": "        pair = tuple(sorted((str(u), str(v))))"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 250,
            "text": "        if pair in path_edges:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 251,
            "text": "            highlighted_edges.append((str(u), str(v)))"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 252,
            "text": "            continue"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 254,
            "text": "        mode = _edge_mode(data)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 255,
            "text": "        if mode == \"transfer\" and not show_transfers:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 256,
            "text": "            continue"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 257,
            "text": "        grouped_edges.setdefault(mode, []).append((str(u), str(v)))"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 259,
            "text": "    edge_traces = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 260,
            "text": "    for mode in (\"bus\", \"tram\", \"metro\", \"rail\", \"other\", \"multi\", \"transfer\"):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 261,
            "text": "        edge_pairs = grouped_edges.get(mode, [])"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 262,
            "text": "        if not edge_pairs:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 263,
            "text": "            continue"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 264,
            "text": "        is_emphasized = highlight_mode is not None and mode == highlight_mode"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 265,
            "text": "        trace = _build_edge_trace("
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 266,
            "text": "            H,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 267,
            "text": "            local_pos,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 268,
            "text": "            edge_pairs,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 269,
            "text": "            color=MODE_COLORS[mode],"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270,
            "text": "            width=3.2 if is_emphasized else 1.6,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 271,
            "text": "            opacity=0.9 if is_emphasized or highlight_mode is None else 0.12,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 272,
            "text": "            name=f\"{mode.title()} edges\","
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 273,
            "text": "        )"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 274,
            "text": "        if trace is not None:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 275,
            "text": "            edge_traces.append(trace)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 276
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 277,
            "text": "    path_trace = _build_edge_trace("
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 278,
            "text": "        H,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 279,
            "text": "        local_pos,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 280,
            "text": "        highlighted_edges,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 281,
            "text": "        color=MODE_COLORS[\"path\"],"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 282,
            "text": "        width=6.0,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 283,
            "text": "        opacity=1.0,"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 284,
            "text": "        name=\"Selected path\","
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 285,
            "text": "    )"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 286,
            "text": "    if path_trace is not None:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 287,
            "text": "        edge_traces.append(path_trace)"
          }
        ],

            "text": "def show_network(G: nx.Graph, pos: dict, max_edges: int = 60000):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17,
            "text": "    edges = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18,
            "text": "    for i, (a, b, data) in enumerate(G.edges(data=True)):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19,
            "text": "        if i \u003e= max_edges:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20,
            "text": "            break"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 21,
            "text": "        edges.append("
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22,
            "text": "            {"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23,
            "text": "                \"a\": str(a),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 24,
            "text": "                \"b\": str(b),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25,
            "text": "                \"edge_kind\": data.get(\"edge_kind\", \"ride\"),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26,
            "text": "                \"mode\": data.get(\"mode\", \"\"),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27,
            "text": "                \"modes\": data.get(\"modes\", \"\"),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28,
            "text": "                \"distance_m\": data.get(\"distance_m\", data.get(\"weight_m\", float(\"nan\"))),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29,
            "text": "                \"time_s\": data.get(\"time_s\", float(\"nan\")),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 30,
            "text": "                \"cost\": data.get(\"cost\", float(\"nan\")),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31,
            "text": "                \"weight_m\": data.get(\"weight_m\", float(\"nan\")),"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32,
            "text": "            }"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 33,
            "text": "        )"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35,
            "text": "    nodes = []"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36,
            "text": "    for n in G.nodes():"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37,
            "text": "        if n in pos:"

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Mapping network edges**

I'm implementing fixed color lookup tables for network edges with fallbacks to mode defaults. </details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


They’re almost all **fixed in code**, not random per feature — but **edges** and **stops** use different rules.

### Edges (lines on the map)
Colors come from constants in `src/viz/plot_mapbox.py`:

- **`MODE_COLORS`** — one hex per coarse type (`bus`, `tram`, `metro`, `rail`, `other`, `multi`, `transfer`, `path`, …).
- **`METRO_LINE_COLORS`**, **`RAIL_LINE_COLORS`**, **`TRAM_LINE_COLORS`** — **per line id** (e.g. Metro `1`, `2`, RER `A`, tram `T3a`) when the geometry’s route name parses to a known key.
- If a line key isn’t in those dicts, it **falls back** to that mode’s default in `MODE_COLORS` (e.g. generic metro purple).

So network lines are **predetermined palettes**; only the **choice** of which constant applies depends on parsed route / mode.

### Nodes (stops / stations)
Stop **fill** uses `MODE_COLORS` again, but the key is **`visible_mode`**, computed per stop from **incident edges** (excluding transfers): one mode → that mode’s color; several modes → `"multi"`; otherwise `"other"`.

```561:571:c:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\src\viz\plot_mapbox.py
def _visible_node_mode(G: nx.Graph, node_id: str) -> str:
    visible_modes: set[str] = set()
    for _u, _v, data in G.edges(node_id, data=True):
        mode = _edge_mode(data)
        if mode != "transfer":
            visible_modes.add(mode)
    if len(visible_modes) == 1:
        return next(iter(visible_modes))
    if len(visible_modes) > 1:
        return "multi"
    return "other"
```

So stops are **not** colored per metro line like the polylines; they’re colored by **that coarse mode / multi** bucket. **Size** also varies with degree (`_node_size`), not with color.

### Product shell map
The iframe from `render_transport_map_html` uses `render_mapbox_gl_html` in the same file; Mapbox layers use **`['get', 'color']`** on GeoJSON properties, and those properties are filled from the same grouping logic above.

**Summary:** Yes — colors are **fixed tables in Python**; edges can vary **by line** where `METRO_LINE_COLORS` / `RAIL_LINE_COLORS` / `TRAM_LINE_COLORS` apply; stop dots use a **small fixed set** tied to inferred stop mode (`multi` / `other` included), not unique per node.

Here’s what changed:

### `TransportMode.tsx`
- Replaced the old “Network stats” label + two rows with a **`section`** that has:
  - Title **`[ NETWORK STATS ]`** as an `<h3>` (accessible heading + `aria-label` on the section)
  - A **two-column grid**: label above value for **Nodes** and **Edges**
  - Same empty state when stats are missing, with a class that matches the card typography

### `transport.css`
- New **`.transport-network-stats`** card: `#050a14` background, `#1a2533` border, monospace stack (`ui-monospace`, Cascadia, Segoe UI Mono, Roboto Mono, …)
- **Title**: muted blue-gray `#7a8ba3`, caps, letter-spacing, bottom rule `#1a2533`
- **Metric labels**: `#4a5a70`, small caps
- **Numbers**: large, heavy `#e0e6ed`, tabular figures, responsive `clamp` for size in the narrow rail

It sits in the same bottom-right float as before, so it reads as a dedicated “network telemetry” block next to Graph / Route. If you want **Roboto Mono** loaded from Google Fonts for a closer match to the mock, we can add a single font link and point the card at it.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was wrong: the top-left float is **`position: absolute`** with **`width: auto`**. In that case the box **sizes to its content**. **`max-width` only sets a ceiling** — it never makes the panel wider than the content, so changing it had no visible effect.

It’s updated to match the right rail pattern: a real **`width`** (still `min(630px, 100% - 32px)`) plus **`box-sizing: border-box`** so padding is included in that width.

After a refresh, the visualization panel should render at **630px** wide on a normal desktop (or the full usable width on narrow viewports).

Here’s what was wrong before and what we changed:

### Why width didn’t feel “full”
The bottom bar used **`left: 50%` + `translateX(-50%)`** and a **fixed `max` width** (`720px`). It never stretched across the map.

### Updates
1. **`.transport-float--bottom`** — `left: 16px`, `right: 16px`, `width: auto`, **`transform` removed** so it spans the map column with **16px** inset on both sides. **`box-sizing: border-box`**. Padding **20px 16px**, gap **20px** (2× the old 10px).

2. **Inputs / buttons** — Roughly **2×** tap targets: input padding **16px 24px**, **16px** type, **12px** radius; Compute/Clear **18px** vertical padding, **12px** type, **12px** radius; focus ring **4px**.

3. **`.transport-suggest-layer`** — Same **16px** side inset as the dock, **`bottom: 116px`** so it sits above the taller bar; **max-height** up to **336px** (2× 168) capped with **`40vh`**; list rows **16px 24px** padding, **14px** text.

The bar is anchored to **`.transport-root`** (the map area next to the rail), so “middle” width is full map width minus **32px** total horizontal inset. Refresh the app to pick up the CSS.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what changed:

### Behavior
The bottom bar and the stop suggestions layer are no longer inset from the **map edges**. They’re inset from the **sides of the HUD**:
- **Left:** `TL offset` + **TL panel width** + **16px** (`--transport-dock-gap`)
- **Right:** `BR offset` + **BR panel width** + **16px**

So the 16px is the gap between the dock and each floating panel, not from the screen.

### Implementation
On **`.transport-root`** there are shared variables:
- `--transport-tl-left` (16px), `--transport-tl-w` (same formula as the top-left panel)
- `--transport-br-right` (14px), `--transport-br-w` (same as the right rail)
- `--transport-dock-gap` (16px)

**`.transport-float--tl`** and **`.transport-float--br`** now use those width/offset variables so the dock math always matches the real panels.

If you change TL/BR width or offsets later, update the variables on `.transport-root` only.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s the distinction:

### Layout (from `AppShell`)
`TransportMode` / `.transport-root` sit only in the **main column** — the **ToolRail** (mode icons) is a **sibling** to the left, not inside the map. So the **left edge of `.transport-root` is already the right edge of that rail**.

### What we changed
The bottom bar and suggestions were still offset as if they had to clear the **top-left floating** “Visualization” card. That was wrong for what you want.

- **Left:** `left: var(--transport-dock-gap)` → **16px in from the main column**, i.e. 16px past the tool rail, **not** past the TL float.
- **Right:** Unchanged: still clears the **right-hand floating** panel + 16px (`BR width + offsets + gap`).

So horizontally: **\[mode rail\] | 16px gap | dock … map … | gap | \[right float\]**.

The TL float can still overlap the dock’s vertical “lane” in the corner; if you want the dock to stay below the TL box only visually, that would be a separate layout tweak.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was added end-to-end.

### Backend
- **`TransportMapRequest`**: optional `selected_stop_id`.
- **`transport_engine.render_transport_map_html`** → passes it into **`render_mapbox_gl_html`**.
- **`_stations_feature_collection`**: if a feature’s `stop_id` matches `selected_stop_id`, it uses **`MODE_COLORS["selected"]`** (orange) and a **larger circle radius** so the stop stands out on the Mapbox GL map.

### Frontend — bottom bar
- **Tabs**: **Route** (existing start/end + Compute + Clear) and **Search stop**.
- **Search stop**: one field (name or ID), **Search** button, **Enter** submits, **Clear highlight** removes selection and reloads the map.
- Same **autocomplete list** as routing (≥2 characters); choosing a row sets the highlighted stop and refreshes the map.
- Status line for errors or **Selected: &lt;stop_id&gt;**.

### Layout CSS
- Bottom float is a **column**: tabs on top, controls row below.
- Suggestions **`bottom`** set to **168px** so they sit above the taller dock.

Restart the product API so the new map field is used. The iframe map is rebuilt on each refresh, so the orange highlight tracks the chosen stop until you clear it or change graph mode (selection is still in React state and resent on refresh).

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Fixing poi family mapping**

I found that `_poi_family` defaults to 'services' for unclassified POI types, but the API wasn't filtering services-only when category_key is None. I discovered that most POI types fall through to return 'services' for display, causing inconsistent UI labeling despite varied underlying categories. 

The _poi_family mapping explains why most POI types show as 'services' in the UI, despite having different underlying categories. The _poi_family mapping assigns most POI types to 'services' family for display, while specific types like shop, tourism, leisure, and transport get their own families. </details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here's what the code is doing.

### API / BallTree filter — **not** forcing “services”

`LocalPOILookup.query` only filters by category when **`category_key`** (and optionally **`category_value`**) is set:

```103:109:c:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\src\core\poi_index.py
        for idx, distance_m in zip(indices, distances_m):
            row = self.df.iloc[int(idx)]
            if category_key is not None and row["category_key"] != category_key:
                continue
            if category_value is not None and row["category_value"] != category_value:
                continue
```

The product-shell map request from **`TransportMode`** does **not** send `poi_category_key`, so the backend passes **`None`** and **every** POI in the parquet (within radius, up to `poi_limit`) can be returned — there is **no** server filter that keeps only “services”.

### Why it still *looks* like “services”

Display uses **`_poi_family`**, which maps each row to a small set of UI buckets (`food`, `shopping`, `tourism`, `leisure`, `transport`, or **`services`**):

```172:186:c:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\src\viz\plot_mapbox.py
def _poi_family(category: Any, category_type: Any) -> str:
    category_text = str(category or "").strip().lower()
    type_text = str(category_type or "").strip().lower()

    if type_text in FOOD_POI_TYPES:
        return "food"
    if category_text == "shop":
        return "shopping"
    if category_text == "tourism":
        return "tourism"
    if category_text == "leisure":
        return "leisure"
    if type_text in TRANSPORT_POI_TYPES:
        return "transport"
    return "services"
```

Anything that isn’t food-like, `shop`, `tourism`, `leisure`, or a listed transport amenity falls through to **`return "services"`**, so you get the grey “building” badge and “services” styling even when the underlying `category_key` / `category_value` in the data is something else (e.g. many `amenity=*` types).

**Summary:** Not filtered to services in the query sense from the web app; the UI **collapses** most POIs into the **services** family by design. To show richer types, you’d extend `_poi_family` (and possibly labels) to use more of `category_key` / `category_value` from the parquet.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
Your `poi.parquet` **does** have a proper **`family`** column (`food`, `shopping`, `tourism`, `leisure`, `transport`, `services`, `other`, …), but **`LocalPOILookup` never loaded it**—it only kept `id`, `name`, `category_key`, `category_value`, `lat`, `lon`.

At the same time, **`category_key` / `category_value` are empty** for those rows. The UI then fell back to `_poi_family()`, which only looks at those fields and amenity lists, so **everything was classified as `services`**.

### Fix
1. **`src/core/poi_index.py`** — If the parquet has a **`family`** column, it’s loaded and returned on each **`query()`** result as `"family"`.
2. **`src/viz/plot_mapbox.py`** — Added **`_poi_badge_from_row`**, which **uses that stored `family`** when choosing icon/color. Parquet **`other`** still uses the neutral “building” style but the label shows **“Other”** instead of “Services”.

After **restarting the API** (so `LocalPOILookup` is recreated), stop popups should again show **Food**, **Shopping**, **Tourism**, etc., in line with the parquet.

**Note:** If the BallTree cache file was built for an older row order, and you ever change the parquet row order without rebuilding the tree, you’d need to regenerate the balltree; that’s unchanged by this fix.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was added and how to use it.

### Backend (FastAPI) — `backend/product_shell/routers/spotify.py`
- **In-memory** token store (`access_token`, `refresh_token`) with a lock.
- **`GET /api/spotify/login-url`** — returns `{ "url": "…" }` (authorize URL).
- **`POST /api/spotify/callback`** — body `{ "code": "<string>" }`, exchanges code for tokens (same redirect URI as Spotify app).
- **`GET /api/spotify/status`** — `{ "connected": true|false }`.
- **`POST /api/spotify/disconnect`** — clears tokens.
- **`POST /api/spotify/play` | `/pause` | `/next`** — Spotify Web API (uses refresh on **401**).
- **Logging**: `cspe.spotify` logs **redirect_uri**, **token exchange status**, and error bodies.

**Env (repo `.env` or process env)**  
- `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`  
- `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`  
- `SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI` — default **`https://localhost:5173/callback`** (must match the Spotify app **exactly**).

**`main.py`** — router mounted at `/api`; CORS extended with **`https://localhost:5173`** and **`https://127.0.0.1:5173`**.

### Frontend (Vite/React)
- **`react-router-dom`**: `/` → `AppShell`, **`/music`** → music UI, **`/callback`** → OAuth finish.
- **`src/pages/MusicPage.tsx`** — Connect, status, Play / Pause / Next, Disconnect.
- **`src/pages/SpotifyCallbackPage.tsx`** — reads `code` (or `error`), **POST** `/api/spotify/callback`, then **navigate to `/music`**.
- **`src/api/spotify.ts`** — thin API helpers.
- **`src/pages/music.css`** — layout/styles.
- **`vite.config.ts`** — **`@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`** + **`https: true`** on port **5173** (needed for the HTTPS redirect URI).
- **`AppShell`** — small **Music** link to `/music`.
- **`run_web_app.ps1`** — reminder to open **`https://localhost:5173`** and configure Spotify.

### Spotify Developer Dashboard
1. Redirect URI: **`https://localhost:5173/callback`** (exact match).  
2. Accept the browser warning for the dev self-signed cert when using Vite HTTPS.

### Flow
1. Open **`https://localhost:5173/music`** → **Connect Spotify** → Spotify login.  
2. Redirect to **`/callback?code=…`** → “Connecting…” → exchange → “Success” → **`/music`**.  
3. **Play / Pause / Next** call Spotify (needs an **active Spotify device** / app).

Tokens are **only in memory**; restarting the API clears them. For Atlas later, you can swap the store for Redis/DB and reuse the same routes.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### 1. **`.env` was loaded too late**
In `main.py`, `from backend.product_shell.routers import … spotify` ran **before** `_load_local_env()`.  
`spotify.py` was reading `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` / `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` **at import time**, so they were always empty → **503** from `_require_config()`.

**Change:** call **`_load_local_env()` first**, then import FastAPI and the routers.

### 2. **Lazy env reads**
Spotify settings are no longer cached at import. They’re read with **`_client_id()`**, **`_client_secret()`**, **`_redirect_uri()`** on each request, so `.env` and env vars are respected even if load order changes again.

---

**You still need credentials in `.env`** (your file only has `MAPBOX_TOKEN` right now). Add:

```env
SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI=https://localhost:5173/callback
```

Restart the product API (`uvicorn`) so it picks up the new `main.py` and `.env`.

If anything is still 503, the response body should say:  
`Spotify not configured: set SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID and SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET…` — that means those two lines are missing or empty.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Why Spotify said `redirect_uri: Insecure`
For **localhost**, Spotify’s policy is to allow **`http://`** redirect URIs. **`https://localhost`** (especially with a dev / self-signed cert) is often treated as **invalid / insecure**, so the authorize or token step fails with that error.

### What we changed
1. **Default redirect** in `spotify.py` → **`http://localhost:5173/callback`**
2. **Vite** → back to **plain HTTP** on 5173 (removed `@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`)
3. **Your `.env`** → `SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI` set to **`http://localhost:5173/callback`**
4. **Music page copy** + **`run_web_app.ps1`** → instructions use **http**, not https
5. Removed the **`@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`** dependency

### What you need to do in Spotify
In the [Spotify Developer Dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard) → your app → **Redirect URIs**:

- **Remove** `https://localhost:5173/callback` if it’s there  
- **Add** **`http://localhost:5173/callback`** (must match **exactly**, including `http`)

Restart the product API and open **`http://localhost:5173/music`** (not `https://`). Then try **Connect Spotify** again.

Spotify’s **current rules** (from [their redirect URI docs](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/concepts/redirect_uri)) are:

- **HTTPS**, **unless** you use a **loopback** address → then **HTTP** is OK.  
- You must use an **explicit IP**: **`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/...`** or **`http://[::1]:PORT/...`**.  
- The hostname **`localhost` is not allowed** (dashboard and API).

So the dashboard is right to block `http://localhost:...` as “not secure” / invalid under the new policy.

### What we changed in the project
- Default + `.env` redirect: **`http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback`**
- Copy on the Music page and in `run_web_app.ps1` updated to match

### What you should do
1. In the Spotify app, add **exactly**:  
   **`http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback`**
2. In `.env`, keep:  
   **`SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI=http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback`**
3. Use the app at **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`** (e.g. **`http://127.0.0.1:5173/music`**) so the origin matches after Spotify sends you back to `127.0.0.1`.
4. Restart the product API after changing `.env`.

You can remove any old **`http://localhost:5173/callback`** entry from the Spotify app; it won’t be accepted for new rules anyway.

### 1. One-time setup
- **Repo root `.env`** (you already have this): `MAPBOX_TOKEN`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI=http://127.0.0.1:5173/callback`.

- **Python deps** (from repo root, in the venv you use for CSPE): `pip install -r requirements.txt` (needs FastAPI, uvicorn, requests, python-dotenv, etc.).
- **Frontend deps** (once):  
  `cd frontend` → `npm install`.

### 2. Start everything (recommended)
From **`C:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE`** in **PowerShell**:

```powershell
.\run_web_app.ps1
```

That script starts (unless you use `-SkipAtlas`) **Atlas**, the **product API** on **8787**, then **Vite** in the foreground.

### 3. Open in the browser
- **Main app:** **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`**  
- **Music / Spotify:** **`http://127.0.0.1:5173/music`**  
  Use **127.0.0.1**, not `localhost`, so it matches Spotify’s redirect URI.

### 4. Stop
In the terminal where Vite is running: **Ctrl+C**. The script cleans up the background API process in its `finally` block.

### Optional flags
- **No Atlas** (if you don’t need chat):  
  `.\run_web_app.ps1 -SkipAtlas`

### If something doesn’t start
- **Product API health:** open **`http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/health`** — should return JSON with `"ok": true`.
- **Manual API** (if you’re not using the script): from repo root with `PYTHONPATH` set to the repo root, run something like:  
  `python -m uvicorn backend.product_shell.main:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787`  
  and in another terminal: `cd frontend` → `npm run dev`.

Here’s what was going on and what to do.

### Why `127.0.0.1:5173` failed while `8787` worked
- **8787** is the **FastAPI** app (started by the script in a background window).
- **5173** is **Vite** and only answers if **`npm run dev`** is running (the **foreground** part of `run_web_app.ps1`).

If you only checked health in the browser but **didn’t** leave the script running through **step [3]** (or you **Ctrl+C**’d Vite), nothing is listening on **5173**.

### Windows + `127.0.0.1` vs `localhost`
Vite’s default **`localhost`** binding can end up on **IPv6 only** (`::1`). Then **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`** never hits the dev server.

**Change made:** `vite.config.ts` now sets **`host: "127.0.0.1"`** and **`strictPort: true`**, so the UI is served on the same host Spotify uses.

### What you should do
1. Stop anything old on 5173 if needed.
2. From repo root run:
   ```powershell
   .\run_web_app.ps1
   ```
3. Wait until you see something like **`VITE v… ready`** and **`Local: http://127.0.0.1:5173/`** (after restart it should show **127.0.0.1**, not only `localhost`).
4. Open **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`** (not `localhost` for Spotify).

**Or** run the API you already use, and in a **second** terminal:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\LEGION\Desktop\CSPE\frontend
npm run dev
```

Then open **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`** again.

If it still fails, say what you see in the terminal after `npm run dev` (any error or “port in use”).

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was added so you can **search** and **start a specific track** from the Music page, on top of your existing controls.

### Backend (`spotify.py`)
- **`GET /api/spotify/search?q=…&limit=…`** — proxies to Spotify’s track search and returns a small list (`id`, `name`, `artists`, `album`, `uri`).
- **`POST /api/spotify/play`** — same as before with **no body / `{}`** = resume; with **`{"uris":["spotify:track:…"]}`** = play that track on the **active** Spotify device.
- **`GET /api/spotify/playback`** — light “now playing” payload for the UI.
- Optional JSON body for play uses **`Body(default=None)`** so clients can POST with an empty body without parse errors.

### Frontend
- Search field + **Search** button, scrollable results; **click a row** → `spotifyPlay([uri])`.
- **Play** still resumes via `spotifyPlay()` with an empty body.
- Line under the status badge shows **now playing** (or a short hint if nothing is active), refreshed every ~8s while connected.

### How to use it
1. Keep Spotify **open somewhere** (desktop app, web player, or phone) so there is an **active device**.
2. On Music, type a query and **Search**; click a track to play it.
3. If you see errors like **no device** or **404**, start playback once in the Spotify app, then try again from CSPE.

No new OAuth scopes were required for search with your current user token. If the API process restarts, you’ll need to **Connect Spotify** again (in-memory tokens).

### What that error means

`{"detail":"Not Found"}` is **FastAPI’s own 404**, not Spotify. It means the HTTP request reached **some** app on **port 8787**, but that app **does not define** the path you called (for example `/api/spotify/search` or `/api/spotify/playback`).

That usually happens when:

1. **An older Product API is still running on 8787** (before the search/playback routes were added). The UI is new; the Python process was never restarted, or a **second** uvicorn is still holding the port.  
2. **Windows `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`**: the dev server was only bound to `127.0.0.1`, so `http://localhost:5173` could hit a **different** process on IPv6 (`::1`) that **does not proxy** `/api` to 8787 the same way.

### What to do

1. **Stop everything** that uses **8787** and **5173** (close `run_web_app.ps1` with Ctrl+C, end stray `python`/`uvicorn` in Task Manager if needed).  
2. Start again from the repo: **`.\run_web_app.ps1`**.  
3. Confirm the API you expect: open **`http://127.0.0.1:8787/docs`** and check for **`GET /api/spotify/search`**.  
4. Optional: open **`http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/health`** — it should include `"spotify_track_search": true` in `capabilities`.

### What we changed in the repo

- **Vite** now uses **`host: true`** so **`http://localhost:5173`** and **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`** use the **same** dev server and **`/api` proxy**.  
- **`/api/health`** now advertises **`capabilities.spotify_track_search`** so the Music page can show a **yellow warning** if 8787 is an old build.  
- Search/play errors that are this FastAPI 404 are turned into a **clear “restart the API on 8787”** message instead of raw JSON.

After a clean restart, search should stop returning that 404. If it persists, say what you see at **`http://127.0.0.1:8787/docs`** (whether Spotify routes appear).

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Checking spotify restrictions**

I'm adding a helper function to handle Spotify's playback restrictions with checks for premium status and active sessions. 

**Handling spotify restrictions**

I'm implementing device ID handling for Spotify playback requests to avoid 403 errors from free tier restrictions. </details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2)**_


Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### 1. Search → `400` / `"Invalid limit"`

Spotify’s **Search** endpoint now documents **`limit` between 0 and 10** (default 5). We were sending **`limit=15`**, which they reject.

**Change:** The backend **caps** `limit` at **10** before calling Spotify, and the frontend default is **10** (Music page no longer passes `15`).

Restart or rely on uvicorn `--reload` and try search again.

---

### 2. Play → `403` / `"Restriction violated"`

That message comes **from Spotify**, not from our routing. Typical causes:

- **Spotify Premium** – Web API playback control usually needs a Premium account.
- **Active device** – Something must be an **active Spotify player** (desktop app, phone app, or [Web Playback SDK](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-playback-sdk) in a browser tab). Open Spotify, start playback once there, then use CSPE.
- **Content rules** – Some tracks or regions block remote start; kids/restricted accounts can block it too.

So: fix search with the limit change; for **403**, check **Premium + a real active device** and try a different track if it keeps happening.

If you want, we can next add **device picking** (list devices from `/me/player/devices` and pass `device_id` on play) to make playback more reliable when several devices show up.

---

_**User**_

it works now instead of having in a whole other page i need it to be in a new page just under map, visual and tasks where we can control music from our ui

---

Here’s what changed:

### Rail (left)
- Added a **fourth mode** with a music icon, **after** Transport → Search and visuals → Memory.
- `AppMode` in `store.ts` now includes `"music"`.

### Main area
- New **`MusicMode`** (`frontend/src/modes/MusicMode.tsx`) is the same Spotify UI (connect, search, play/pause/next, disconnect, now playing), laid out like the other modes with `mode-page` / `mode-page__main`.
- **Embedded styling** via `music-page--embedded` + `music-mode__main` so it sits on the shell background instead of the old full-page gradient.
- Removed the bottom **“Music”** link from `AppShell`.

### Routes
- **`/music`** only switches to Music mode and **`replace`s to `/`** (so old bookmarks still work).
- **`/callback`** still handles OAuth, then sets mode to **music** and goes to **`/`** (not `/music`).
- Removed the standalone **`MusicPage`** component.

### Files touched
- `store.ts`, `ToolRail.tsx`, `AppShell.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `SpotifyCallbackPage.tsx`, `music.css`
- Added: `modes/MusicMode.tsx`
- Deleted: `pages/MusicPage.tsx`

Use the **music note** on the rail to open Music; after Spotify login you’ll land on home with **Music** already selected.

          {
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 115,
            "text": "### 4) The orchestrator opens an OpenAI Realtime WebSocket session"

          },

          {
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 129,
            "text": "Local-only greeting:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {

          {
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 133,
            "text": "### 5) Microphone audio is streamed to OpenAI (but locally captured)"

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 137,
            "text": "Three async tasks run during a session:"

          {
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {

            "text": "async def sender(ws, state: CallState):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 96,
            "text": "    \"\"\"Send audio from queue to websocket in batches.\"\"\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 97,
            "text": "    buffer = bytearray()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98,
            "text": "    last_send = time.monotonic()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99,
            "text": "    _stop_event = get_stop_event()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 100,
            "text": "    "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101,
            "text": "    while state.running and not _stop_event.is_set():"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 102,
            "text": "        try:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 103,
            "text": "            pcm = await asyncio.wait_for(state.queue.get(), timeout=0.05)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 104,
            "text": "            buffer.extend(pcm)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 105,
            "text": "        except asyncio.TimeoutError:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 106,
            "text": "            pass"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 107
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 108,
            "text": "        now = time.monotonic()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 109,
            "text": "        if buffer and (len(buffer) \u003e= APPEND_BATCH_BYTES or (now - last_send) \u003e= 0.15):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 110,
            "text": "            await ws.send(json.dumps({"
          },

            "text": "                \"type\": \"input_audio_buffer.append\","
          },
          {

            "text": "                \"audio\": base64.b64encode(buffer).decode(\"ascii\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 113,

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 114,
            "text": "            buffer.clear()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 115,
            "text": "            last_send = now"
          },
          {
            "isSignature": true,
            "lineNumber": 116,
            "text": "        await asyncio.sleep(0.005)"

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 269
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270,

          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 273
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 274,
            "text": "## Side effects (everything that touches the outside world)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 275
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 276,
            "text": "### Network"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 277
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 278,
            "text": "- **OpenAI Realtime** (WebSocket): &#96;core/orchestrator.py&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 279,
            "text": "  - sends: &#96;session.update&#96;, &#96;input_audio_buffer.append&#96;, &#96;response.create&#96;, and &#96;conversation.item.create&#96; (reinjection)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 280,
            "text": "  - receives: VAD events, transcription completed, response deltas, response.done, error events"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 281,
            "text": "- **SerpAPI** (HTTP):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 282,
            "text": "  - Google Web Search: &#96;clients/serpapi_client.google_search()&#96; used by &#96;tools/web_search.py&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 283,
            "text": "  - Google Images: &#96;clients/serpapi_client.google_images()&#96; used by API &#96;/image-search&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 284,
            "text": "- **YouTube Data API v3** (HTTP):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 285,
            "text": "  - &#96;audio/music_player._search_youtube()&#96; uses &#96;YOUTUBE_API_KEY&#96;"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 286,
            "text": "- **UI image proxy**:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 287,
            "text": "  - Flask endpoint &#96;/image-proxy&#96; fetches arbitrary image URLs and streams bytes back to browser UI"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 288
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 289,
            "text": "### Audio I/O"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 290
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 291,
            "text": "- **Microphone capture**:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 292,

          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 296,

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 1,
            "text": "# PROJECT ATLAS — High-level Mental Model (from code)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 3,
            "text": "## What this project is"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 5,
            "text": "**ATLAS** is a local, Windows-first “voice assistant shell” that runs as **three cooperating processes**:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 7,
            "text": "- **ATLAS API**: a Flask server that hosts the UI, exposes control endpoints (&#96;/wake&#96;, &#96;/sleep&#96;, &#96;/shutdown&#96;), and starts/stops the “session” (the assistant runtime) in a background thread."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 8,
            "text": "- **Wake Service**: a lightweight always-on microphone listener using **Vosk** offline speech recognition to detect fixed wake/sleep phrases and POSTs to the API."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 9,
            "text": "- **ATLAS UI**: a desktop window using **pywebview** that displays a Three.js visualization, the latest user/assistant text, and optional image panels by polling the API."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 11,
            "text": "The “assistant brain” is implemented as an **async realtime session** that connects to the **OpenAI Realtime WebSocket API** (&#96;wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime&#96;) and streams microphone audio to server-side VAD + transcription; responses are rendered as text in the UI and spoken **locally** via **Azure Cognitive Services TTS** (the model is configured for &#96;modalities=[\"text\"]&#96;)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 13,
            "text": "Separately, a “pulse” subsystem provides a live **visual intensity meter** for the UI driven by UDP audio-like samples emitted during TTS playback."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15,
            "text": "## Repository layout (what lives where)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17,
            "text": "- &#96;start_atlas.bat&#96;: primary launcher; starts API, wake service, then UI."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18,
            "text": "- &#96;atlas.env&#96;: dotenv-style env file loaded by the app (contains API keys in this repo; treat as secrets)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/&#96;: main application package (API, orchestrator, tools, UI state, audio, storage)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20,
            "text": "- &#96;src/wake_service/&#96;: wake-word process (Vosk + sounddevice)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 21,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/ui/static/index.html&#96;: the entire “frontend” (pure HTML/JS)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/router/&#96;: tool registry (&#96;tools_registry.json&#96;) and executor (&#96;tool_executor.py&#96;)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/tools/&#96;: tool implementations (web search, images/visual board, memory, music)."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 24,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/storage/&#96;: SQLite persistence for “memory” items."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25,
            "text": "- &#96;src/atlas_client/audio/&#96;: Azure TTS and music playback."
          }
        ],
        "range": {
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 25
          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 654,
            "text": "        # Mutable runtime state for event handlers"

          {

            "lineNumber": 665
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 666,
            "text": "        async def mode_watcher():"
          },
          {

            "text": "            \"\"\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 668,
            "text": "            Hot-switch between voice and text modes without restarting the session."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 669,
            "text": "            - voice: mic + sender running"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 670,
            "text": "            - text: mic + sender cancelled"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 671,
            "text": "            \"\"\""
          },

          },

            "text": "            _stop = get_stop_event()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 674,
            "text": "            while not _stop.is_set():"
          },
          {

            "text": "                await asyncio.sleep(0.25)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 676,
            "text": "                desired = (get_input_mode() or \"voice\").strip().lower()"

          {
            "lineNumber": 677,
            "text": "                if desired not in (\"voice\", \"text\"):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 678,
            "text": "                    desired = \"voice\""
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 679,
            "text": "                if desired == mode:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 680,
            "text": "                    continue"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 681
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 682,
            "text": "                mode = desired"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 683,
            "text": "                if mode == \"text\":"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 684,
            "text": "                    LOG.info(\"[InputMode] switched -\u003e text (microphone disabled)\")"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 685,
            "text": "                    for t in (mic_task, send_task):"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 686,
            "text": "                        if not t:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 687,
            "text": "                            continue"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 688,
            "text": "                        try:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 689,
            "text": "                            t.cancel()"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 690,
            "text": "                        except Exception:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 691,

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 692,
            "text": "                    mic_task = None"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 693,

          },

            "text": "                else:"

            "text": "                    if not mic_task:"
